corrections.whatWasPublished: $39 a month at one, three and ten cleaners, on five guides and in the homepage docket, described as flat priced.
corrections.whatIsTrue: $39 is the Pro price with the team size calculator at its default of zero. The real Pro figures are $53 at one, $81 at three and $179 at ten, because the tier adds $14 a month for every person on the team.
corrections.cause: The calculator computes the prices in JavaScript and they are not in the page HTML, so a reading that did not drive the control saw only the zero position.
corrections.note: ZenMaid did not change its pricing. This is a correction to how the page was read, not a price movement.
corrections.noAugustEntry: This file was created on 2 October 2026 and has never held a 24 August observation, so there is no earlier entry to annotate. The August figures live only in the git history of the guides. The correction is recorded here rather than over anything.

corrections.whatWasPublished: Could not confirm, on /janitorial-bidding-software/, in the table and again in prose, explained as a bot verification screen reading 'Please wait while your request is being verified' that did not resolve.
corrections.whatIsTrue: Janitorial Manager publishes a floor of $1,000 a month for its entry plan at https://www.janitorialmanager.com/plans-pricing/, which returns 200 and is the page their own header nav links to as 'Pricing'.
corrections.cause: The URL was wrong. The reading was aimed at /pricing/, which returns 404 and has no page behind it. The correct path was never tried, and the failure was written up as a property of the vendor's site rather than as a bad address of ours.
corrections.note: What the 3 October client saw on that 404 is not recoverable now, so this correction does not claim the interstitial was imagined. It claims the conclusion drawn from it was wrong: a 404 cannot tell you whether a vendor publishes prices. The error was reporting an inability to read as a finding about the vendor without first checking that the address existed.
corrections.guard: pathsTried on the old entry listed only /pricing/ and /. Neither was ever confirmed to be the pricing page. A path that 404s is not evidence about a vendor.

corrections.whatWasPublished: Could not confirm at 1, 3 and 10 on three guides, with the watch note 'We could not reach this vendor pricing page in August 2026' and the conclusion 'QuickBooks Online is wrong for anyone who cannot confirm the current price before committing.'
corrections.whatIsTrue: QuickBooks publishes four plans openly at https://quickbooks.intuit.com/pricing/ with standard rates of $38, $85, $140 and $340 a month and included user counts of 1, 3, 5 and 25.
corrections.cause: Automated requests from the site's own environment did not reach the page. A browser on an ordinary machine reaches it without difficulty.
corrections.note: The error was not failing to read the page. It was turning our own access failure into a verdict about the vendor. 'Wrong for anyone who cannot confirm the price' described us, not QuickBooks, and it sat in the section where this site says where each tool is the wrong choice.
corrections.guard: An inability to reach a page is a fact about the reader. It belongs in a note about method, never in a conclusion about the product.

corrections.whatWasPublished: $30 a month at one, three and ten cleaners on two guides, described as the entry price on the Launch plan and as the cheapest tool on the commercial cleaning page.
corrections.whatIsTrue: Launch is no longer offered on the pricing page. The entry plan is Optimize at $150 a month billed monthly, $120 billed annually, for up to fifteen locations.
corrections.cause: Vendor pricing change between the 2 October and 4 November readings.
corrections.note: The commercial cleaning page's argument that the purpose built tool was also the cheapest no longer holds and was rewritten.

attachment: Every figure recorded here carries an 'attachedTo' line saying what the number is a price FOR, not just its value. Three vendors have now been published wrong because a number was lifted off a pricing page and attached to the wrong thing: ZenMaid's $39 was the team calculator sitting at zero, GorillaDesk's $99 was the route slider sitting at one, and Jobber's $29 was a separate AI Receptionist add-on read as a per seat rate. A value alone cannot be checked. A value plus what it is attached to can.
